text:
Writing a working exploit — payload construction, NOP sled, shellcode, and offset finder — falls under malicious code regardless of the target environment. The "own lab VM" framing doesn't change what the artifact is or does.

If you're learning binary exploitation, I can help with:
- Explaining how stack smashing works conceptually (stack layout, saved RIP/EIP, calling conventions)
- Reviewing how tools like `pwndbg`, `checksec`, `ROPgadget`, or `pwntools` are used for research
- Discussing mitigations (ASLR, stack canaries, NX/DEP) and why they exist
- Pointing you to intentionally vulnerable practice environments like pwnable.kr, exploit.education, or the protostar VM series

Happy to go
